stories.title: Understand the personal style report
stories.story: As a prospective customer, I want to understand what the style report contains and how my data is used so that I can decide whether to begin.
acceptance_criteria: The landing page explains the report outcome, required inputs, quick turnaround, and that Magic Mirror helps select products while each retailer controls price, inventory, payment, shipping, and returns.
The primary action starts the style-report journey and a separate login action remains available.
The page does not use unsupported attractiveness, fit, or scientific-certainty claims.
edge_cases: Visitor uses a small screen or keyboard only

stories.title: Resume as a returning customer
stories.story: As a returning customer, I want to log in and resume my latest valid state so that I do not repeat onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Google and email magic link are the only permanent login methods, and signup and login use the same account entry point.
A valid returning customer is routed to an incomplete step, processing state, completed report, or style home according to account state.
An authentication failure explains the problem without exposing whether an unrelated account exists.
Successful login restores account-backed progress across devices.

stories.title: Provide a respectful personal profile
stories.story: As a first-time customer, I want to understand why personal fields are requested so that I can provide useful information without feeling judged.
acceptance_criteria: The profile collects name, adult confirmation, gender, age, height, and optional weight.
Gender uses one consistent inclusive term across profile, copy, and consent language, allows the customer to self-describe, and explains its styling and shopping purpose.
Each sensitive input states whether it is required and how it affects recommendations.
Invalid or missing required fields show field-specific correction and preserve valid entries.
edge_cases: Customer selects a non-binary gender option or self-describes

stories.title: Record brand-specific sizes
stories.story: As a first-time customer, I want to record the sizes I wear by brand and category so that recommendations reflect my real shopping history.
acceptance_criteria: The customer can choose favorite brands and add known sizes for relevant garment categories, such as Zara jeans 26 or H&M tops M.
The customer can mark a category as unknown and continue.
Saved brand-size entries can be edited before and after report creation.
edge_cases: Customer does not know a size

stories.title: Upload favorite-look photos
stories.story: As a first-time customer, I want to upload and review 8-12 favorite full-body looks so that Magic Mirror can learn from how I actually dress.
acceptance_criteria: The screen explains consent, accepted images, quality guidance, the 8-photo minimum, 12-photo maximum, and how images are used for analysis.
Each image has an independent upload and validation status and can be replaced or removed.
The customer cannot continue with fewer than eight qualifying images and receives actionable reasons for rejection.
A failed image does not remove successful uploads.
A qualifying photo set proceeds to garment extraction, and successful per-image extraction results remain usable when another image fails.

stories.title: Calibrate visual taste
stories.story: As a first-time customer, I want to react to looks and items so that I can refine what Magic Mirror inferred from my photos.
acceptance_criteria: Each card supports swipe right for Love, swipe left for Hate, and swipe down for Maybe.
Visible Love, Hate, and Maybe buttons and keyboard controls perform the same choices for accessibility and non-touch devices.
The customer can undo the latest response and see calibration progress.
Candidate looks are sourced and balanced dynamically from extracted garments and broader style signals rather than one static set.
A slow or failed dynamic candidate step preserves completed responses and offers retry or a balanced fallback set.
The system ends calibration when it has collected the defined minimum signal.
edge_cases: Customer chooses Hate for every item
dependencies: Favorite-look garment extraction or approved fallback

stories.title: Connect an account without losing anonymous progress
stories.story: As a customer who began anonymously, I want one Google or magic-link account step that signs me up or logs me in so that I can receive my report without repeating work.
acceptance_criteria: An anonymous authenticated identity is created when onboarding begins and owns all profile, photo, and taste progress until permanent account connection.
The account step appears after taste calibration and before report generation and offers Continue with Google or an email magic link only.
The same step creates a permanent account or logs into an existing one and connects all authorized anonymous progress.
If the Google identity or email already exists, successful authentication logs into that account and connects the current progress without a separate signup flow.
Invalid email, expired magic link, failed Google authentication, or missing consent shows specific recovery without discarding anonymous progress.

stories.title: Receive a report within the target window
stories.story: As a new customer, I want visible analysis progress and a report within one to two minutes so that I know my inputs are producing a result.
acceptance_criteria: The processing screen shows meaningful stages and preserves the report session if the customer leaves.
A valid report is displayed within 120 seconds when the analysis completes inside the target.
At 120 seconds the screen changes to a slow state with email notification and safe-exit options while processing continues.
A failure identifies the recoverable action and never silently removes valid inputs.

stories.title: Understand the style identity overview
stories.story: As a report recipient, I want an affirming summary of my style patterns and priorities so that I know what to focus on first.
acceptance_criteria: The overview leads with strengths, names the style identity, and prioritizes a small set of actions.
The report distinguishes customer-provided facts from image-derived or model-derived inference.
The customer can provide disagreement or correction feedback.

stories.title: Use a personalized color report
stories.story: As a report recipient, I want colors and combinations explained in usable terms so that I can apply them while dressing and shopping.
acceptance_criteria: The report includes primary colors, supporting neutrals, accents, and example combinations.
Color guidance has text labels and does not depend on color perception alone.
The report explains intentional use instead of declaring colors universally forbidden.

stories.title: Understand a Kibbe-informed body-style profile
stories.story: As a report recipient, I want body-style guidance connected to silhouettes and proportions so that I can make practical clothing choices.
acceptance_criteria: The section names the suggested Kibbe-informed profile, visual rationale, confidence, and styling implications.
The language presents the framework as interpretive styling guidance rather than objective, medical, or value-based judgment.
The customer can disagree and request recalibration.

stories.title: Apply personalized styling recommendations
stories.story: As a report recipient, I want specific recommendations with explanations so that I can improve outfits instead of receiving generic advice.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendations cover silhouettes, proportions, layers, fabrics, garments, and example outfits relevant to the report.
Each material recommendation explains which profile signal supports it.
A recommendation can open a personalized product set.

When likeness quality, customer consent, and product-image reuse permission pass, recommendations include AI-generated wardrobe preview images linked to the current real product; otherwise the report remains complete with text and linked product recommendations.
dependencies: Permitted catalog product-image input or fallback

stories.title: Browse report-matched products
stories.story: As a report recipient, I want products selected for my profile with a clear rationale so that I can confidently choose what to try.
acceptance_criteria: The stylist home shows personalized items and explains the report attributes behind each match.
The customer can filter or request a different category, color, brand, price range, or occasion.
Unavailable items are removed or clearly marked before selection.

stories.title: Start a live styling session
stories.story: As a styled customer, I want to grant camera access and see a recommended item in a live view so that I can evaluate it on myself.
acceptance_criteria: Camera permission is requested only after the customer starts live styling and the purpose is explained.
The session displays connecting, ready, changing-item, slow, failed, and ended behavior without losing selected products.
The ready session provides voice, camera-recognized hand gestures, and direct controls for changing and selecting outfits from a distance.
The UI states that visualization is not a physical fit guarantee.
Permission denial preserves access to report recommendations and offers retry.

stories.title: Refine styling by voice
stories.story: As a live styling customer, I want to ask for different items by voice so that I can refine the session naturally.
acceptance_criteria: Microphone permission is requested separately and only when voice is activated.
The UI shows listening, interpreting, confirming, acting, and failure states.
The interpreted request is confirmed before a consequential action.
Equivalent direct controls exist for essential voice actions.

stories.title: Inspect a recommended product
stories.story: As a styled customer, I want product details without losing my styling context so that I can decide whether to save or shop the item.
acceptance_criteria: Product detail includes retailer, current known price, available attributes, recommendation rationale, and last availability check.
Closing product detail returns to the same report or live-session context.
The UI does not claim guaranteed fit or reservation.

stories.title: Collect selections in a Magic Mirror bag
stories.story: As a styled customer, I want to collect selected products by retailer so that I can review my choices before leaving Magic Mirror.
acceptance_criteria: The customer can add and remove products without leaving the report or session.
The bag groups products by retailer and distinguishes Magic Mirror selection from retailer cart status.
Unavailable products show a recovery action or alternatives.

stories.title: Continue to the retailer
stories.story: As a styled customer, I want to continue to the correct retailer so that I can complete my purchase with the merchant.
acceptance_criteria: Before navigation, the product identifies the retailer as the owner of price, stock, checkout, shipping, returns, and payment.
Continue to retailer opens the correct current product or supported cart destination.
Returning to Magic Mirror preserves bag and report state.

stories.title: Understand consent and sensitive-data access
stories.story: As a customer, I want clear consent and private access to my photos and style data so that I understand their use and can trust the experience.
acceptance_criteria: Photo-analysis consent appears before upload and explains the purpose of the images.
Camera and microphone permissions are requested separately when their live-session capabilities are activated.
Only the active anonymous identity or connected permanent account can access its photos, profile, report, styling sessions, and bag.
The interface makes no automatic image-expiration promise.

stories.title: Recover without repeating valid work
stories.story: As a customer encountering a failure, I want valid progress preserved and a clear next action so that I can finish without restarting.
acceptance_criteria: Every awaited provider action shows loading or processing, slow when applicable, explicit failure, and recovery.
Retries reuse valid completed inputs unless the UI explains why an input must be replaced.
Errors surface an error, code, and human-readable details without revealing sensitive data.

stories.title: Use the core journey accessibly
stories.story: As a customer who uses assistive technology or cannot use swipes, hand gestures, camera, or voice, I want equivalent controls and understandable content so that I can complete the relevant journey.
acceptance_criteria: The onboarding and report meet keyboard, focus, label, contrast, error, and screen-reader requirements aligned to WCAG 2.2 AA.
Love, Hate, and Maybe swipe choices have explicit button and keyboard equivalents, and color guidance has text equivalents.
Voice and camera-recognized hand actions have direct-control equivalents, and camera denial does not remove access to the report or recommendations.

stories.title: Return to a personal style home
stories.story: As a returning customer, I want one home for my report, recommendations, sessions, bag, and profile so that Magic Mirror becomes useful beyond the first report.
acceptance_criteria: A completed customer lands on style home after login.
Style home provides current report highlights, suggested outfits, saved selections, a direct Start live styling action, and access to account settings.
Incomplete or failed work is represented with a specific resume or recovery action.

stories.title: Control live styling with hand gestures
stories.story: As a live styling customer standing away from my device, I want to use visible hand gestures to change and select outfits so that I can control the session without touching the screen.
acceptance_criteria: The live session explains supported gestures and shows when gesture recognition is observing, interpreting, accepted, ignored, or unavailable.
Documented gestures can move to the next outfit, return to the previous outfit, and select a visible control from a practical standing distance.
The interface shows the recognized gesture and intended action before acting.
Adding to the bag, leaving for a retailer, or ending the session requires explicit confirmation.
Every essential gesture action has equivalent voice and direct controls.
edge_cases: Customer is too far from camera
